summary: Exhaustive prior-art sweep completed and cross-checked against our 2026 corpus. Two open-source byte-level projects exist: phi-ag/rvt (TypeScript, MIT — CFB reader + a real BasicFileInfo grammar + thumbnail; ships an 11-release RFA corpus) and DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs (Rust, Apache-2, ~55K lines — Formats/Latest schema parser with u16 class tags and 100% field-type classification, ElemTable/ContentDocuments/PartitionTable/Contents/Partitions-header decoders, tag-drift dataset, partial ADocument walker, one decoded 2023 ArcWall record, byte-preserving writer; its own docs concede element extraction from real files is unsolved). A 2025 ZDI exploit write-up independently establishes that Revit streams end in a gzip trailer + zero padding + ECC trailer that Revit verifies/repairs (Utility.dll), and that the deserializer is a u16 class-index scheme (4,611 classes in 2025). Verifying these claims on our six files exposed a critical gap in KNOWLEDGE.md: the gzip trailer is present and valid on small streams, but our raw-inflate output for large streams (Formats/Latest, Global/Latest, ContentDocuments, big ElemTables) mismatches the writer's CRC32/ISIZE by ~0.45% and the inflated Formats/Latest is visibly corrupted past ~0x22000 — decompression of large streams is unsolved. Also fetched two redistributable corpora into vendor/ (11 phi-ag RFAs; magnetar-io 2023/2024 project files with their own IFC exports = a decoding oracle) and confirmed .rfa/.rte/.rft share the container, differing only in PartAtom (family, plain XML) vs ProjectInformation (project, ZIP-wrapped project.xml), Partitions/N multiplicity, and ElemTable/PartitionTable framing.
key_findings: The 'phi-ag/rvt Rust project' in the brief conflates two things: phi-ag/rvt is TypeScript (npm @phi-ag/rvt, Peter Hirn, MIT) parsing only CFB + BasicFileInfo + preview PNG; the deep Rust reader is DrunkOnJava/rvt-rs (Griffin Long, Apache-2, built 2026-04). Both cloned to vendor/.

rvt-rs is the state of the art: Formats/Latest class-record grammar ([u16 len][name][u16 tag|0x8000][pad][parent][ancestor_tag][u32 fc][u32 fc][fields with u32 name prefix + type-encoding block]), a complete field type-encoding table (0x01 bool…0x0e ref/vector/container, alt string 08 60 00 00, deprecated 0x03), an 11-release tag-drift CSV, Global/Latest framing (upgrade-history strings + two sequential-id tables + schema-referenced instance mass; instances are tag-less schema-directed), ElemTable 12/28/40-byte record variants, ContentDocuments 40-byte linked list (2024), Global/PartitionTable + Contents + 44-byte Partitions header decodes, partition tag-density methodology, and a Revit-2023-only ArcWall record decode. Its explicit failures: no ElementId→location index, no element extraction on real files, ADocument walk validated only 2024–2026.

CRITICAL: our compression model is wrong/incomplete. Every gzip'd stream ends with [u32 CRC32][u32 ISIZE][zero padding][variable trailing block] (ZDI 2025 calls the last part an ECC trailer that Revit uses to auto-repair/verify streams, routines in Utility.dll). Small streams validate perfectly (e.g. racbasic Global/History CRC 0xa3525784/ISIZE 15,290; Global/ElemTable 0xeb4f97d1/336,070), but Formats/Latest (ISIZE 496,597 vs 498,766 inflated), every Global/Latest, ContentDocuments and large ElemTables mismatch by ~0.45%, and inflated Formats/Latest shows LZ77-desync garbling from ~0x22000 despite a fully standard deflate bitstream (verified with a pure-Python inflater: 10 blocks, max distance 32,505, no Deflate64 codes). Correct decoding of large streams is UNSOLVED; several extracted streams (dach ElemTable/ContentDocuments, rme ElemTable, racadv ContentDocuments) fail to inflate at all and are missing from extracted/.

Independent confirmation of the object model: ZDI (Revit 2025) — the deserializer reads a u16 class index, 4,611 serializable classes are registered via Utility!ArchiveClassMaps::loadClass / ARuntimeClass::createObject, AString = index 0x1f, strings are length-prefixed; rvt-rs cross-checked schema class names against exported RevitAPI.dll symbols. So Formats/Latest is the on-disk archive class map (Rosetta stone confirmed; expect thousands of classes — rvt-rs's 64 KB scan cap and its ~400-class count are artefacts of the decompression problem).

Sibling formats: .rfa/.rte/.rft use the identical CFB container and stream inventory. Differences: families have PartAtom (plain Atom XML, urn:schemas-autodesk-com:partatom, 'application/rfa') and exactly one Partitions/N (N increments per upgrade of the same file: 58 in 2016 → 69 in 2026); projects have ProjectInformation (ZIP wrapping <Temp>\Revit<guid>.project.xml in the same partatom namespace — KNOWLEDGE.md's hypothesis confirmed, wording wrong) and may carry many Partitions/N streams (magnetar 2023: 0–6; 2024: 46–65; our dach: 84,85). RevitPreview4.0 is optional (absent in rstbasicsampleproject).

Verified prior-art claims on our 2026 files with byte evidence: BasicFileInfo fileVersion=14 at offset 0 and the 04 00 00 00 marker + length-prefixed UTF-16 strings (phi-ag grammar holds on projects); Formats/Latest first record 'A3PartyAImage' with tag word 0x800d (rvt-rs stable tag 0x000d); ElemTable header u16 element_count=1481/record_count=8401 with FF×8 markers at 0x22 stride 40 (rvt-rs project-2024 layout = phi-ag's 40-byte hypothesis); Partitions/15 first gzip at offset 44 (44-byte header); Global/PartitionTable = 87-byte project variant with per-release counter 3200 and a UUIDv1 {e3e052f8-0156-11d5-9301-0000863f27ad} sharing the …0000863f27ad node with rvt-rs's family GUID.

New redistributable corpora fetched (LFS objects sha256-verified): phi-ag's 11 rac_basic_sample_family RFAs (2016–2026, CC-BY-NC-SA) and magnetar-io/revit-test-datasets (MIT: Revit_IFC5_Einhoven.rvt 2023, 2024_Core_Interior.rvt 34 MB, 4 RFAs, and IFC exports of the same model — a ground-truth oracle for element decoding that no prior project had wired up).

Format identification prior art: PRONOM x-fmt/443–448 and container-signature PUIDs fmt/1346–1351 with concrete DROID container signatures (Formats + BasicFileInfo streams; UTF-16LE 'Revit Build:' ≤2018 / 'Author: Autodesk Revit\r' near EOF 2019+; PartAtom containing 'application/rfa' for families); Just Solve wiki records era history (Revit 4–9 had no BasicFileInfo). Official closed-file read/write surfaces exist for BasicFileInfo (BasicFileInfo.Extract) and TransmissionData (Read/WriteTransmissionData) — usable as codec oracles.
confidence: High for the bibliography, the rvt-rs/phi-ag capability inventories and porting map, the sibling-format equivalence, and the byte-level verifications (all reproduced today with offsets on our corpus). High that KNOWLEDGE.md's 'corrupt gzip trailer' claim is wrong (valid CRC32/ISIZE demonstrated on multiple streams). Medium on the interpretation of the large-stream decompression divergence (the fact of the mismatch and the garbling is certain; the mechanism — ECC-repair-required perturbation vs. writer-side framing — is a labelled hypothesis). Low confidence in rvt-rs's claim that Apache Tika reads BasicFileInfo (unverified). ZDI's ECC/class-index facts are from a reputable primary source but were established on Revit 2025, not 2026.", "note": ""
open_questions: What exactly makes standard raw-inflate diverge on large streams (Formats/Latest, Global/Latest, ContentDocuments, ElemTable > ~350 KB inflated) while validating perfectly (CRC32+ISIZE) on smaller ones — is the payload deliberately perturbed and repaired via the ECC trailer (per ZDI), does the writer exclude in-band framing from its CRC/ISIZE, or does the trailing block carry fix-up data? The fixed oracle is Formats/Latest: correct output must be 496,597 bytes with CRC32 0x26852216.

Structure and algorithm of the post-deflate trailing block (37–350 bytes, not size-proportional; 91 bytes recurs) and the zero-padding rule; ZDI says the ECC/gzip routines and diagnostic strings live in Utility.dll — needs a Windows/Revit install to confirm.

How many classes are really in Formats/Latest once decoding is fixed (rvt-rs sees ~400 with a 64 KB cap; ZDI reports 4,611 registered classes in Revit 2025), and does the class tag order in the stream equal the runtime u16 class index (AString = 0x1f)?

Semantics of the 44-byte Partitions/N header (rvt-rs refuted 'trailer u32s = chunk offsets'), of the sequential-id Tables A/B at the top of Global/Latest, and of the ElemTable payload ints — none map ElementId → data location yet.

Whether Revit 2026 project files' ContentDocuments follows the 2024 40-byte u64 linked-list layout (our head shows 2023-style u32 id pairs) and whether the 2023-only ArcWall record layout has an equivalent in 2026 partitions.
Whether a writer can emit streams Revit accepts without reproducing the ECC trailer (ZDI's experience with Global/Latest says no; small streams also carry trailing blocks).
next_steps: Compression agent: take docs/inbox/prior-art-corrections.md §1 as its brief — return and validate the [CRC32][ISIZE] trailer, decode the zero-pad + trailing block, and crack correct decoding of large streams using Formats/Latest (CRC32 0x26852216, ISIZE 496,597) as the oracle; re-extract dach ElemTable/ContentDocuments, rme ElemTable, racadv ContentDocuments which currently have no carved members.

Schema agent: port rvt-rs formats.rs (parse_schema, FieldType::decode/encode, tagged-class preamble) to src/rvt/schema.py without the 64 KB scan cap, using rvt-rs's 30+ pinning unit tests as vectors; ship the tag-drift CSV with attribution; re-derive the class inventory on our six 2026 files once decompression is fixed.

Metadata agent: port phi-ag src/info.ts (BasicFileInfo grammar, versions 10/13/14) to Python with node.test.ts golden values as tests; add ProjectInformation (ZIP + project.xml) and PartAtom parsing (port rvt-rs part_atom.rs), the 62 19 22 05 Contents/RevitPreview4.0 wrapper, and TransmissionData round-trip against the official API semantics.

Orchestrator: merge the KNOWLEDGE.md rewrites in the corrections note (§1 compression, §2 PartAtom/ProjectInformation, §3 8-byte prefix + 62 19 22 05 wrappers, §4 Partitions 44-byte header/multiple partitions/chunk-boundary non-semantics, §5 corpus gaps) and add the magnetar corpus (with its IFC oracle) to the sample set.

Element/partition agents: read vendor/rvt-rs/reports/element-framing/RE-*.md and docs/rvt-moat-break-reconnaissance.md before probing (20+ refuted hypotheses catalogued); adopt the tag-density + [tag][00 00] record-prefix filter methodology and the concrete-class model (ArcWall/VWall, not Wall).

Writer track: plan for ECC-trailer recomputation; consider thezdi/CompoundFileTool for CFB explode/rebuild experiments and rvt-rs writer.rs/cfb-structural-layout notes (CFB v4, 4 KB sectors, miniFAT at sector 2).
